findings.summary: NoisyTCP is an 11-year-old Linux kernel bug . It lets a remote attacker crash a server without logging in. The flaw is tracked as CVE-2026-99288. Hyunwoo Kim (@v4bel) reported and patched it, and he released the NoisyTCP advisory on GitHub after the Linux distribution embargo ended. The flaw sits in the kernel’s TCP code, which handles almost all network traffic on Linux. Kim says it can be triggered against plain TCP listeners.
findings.title: NoisyTCP: 11-Year-Old Linux Kernel Flaw Lets Unauthenticated Attackers Crash Servers Remotely

findings.summary: Apple has patched a privacy bug in iOS, iPadOS, and macOS that let an app record microphone audio after the user said no. The flaw is tracked as CVE-2026-65339. On an earlier iOS 27 beta build, the orange microphone dot stayed off, and the system logs did not name the app. Apple’s own note was short. It said only that “an app may be able to leak sensitive user information ” and that “a logic issue was addressed with improved checks”. That wording hides how serious the bug was.

findings.summary: Claude users can connect VirusTotal threat intelligence to their investigations, bringing file, URL, domain, and IP reports into an AI workflow. The connection lets analysts review detection findings, analysis dates, coverage, and source links without treating an AI answer as a security verdict. The integration uses Model Context Protocol, or MCP, to connect Claude with VirusTotal AI, known as VTAI. Users authenticate through browser OAuth without providing a personal VirusTotal API key.

findings.summary: ### Summary `Request.post()` had no limit on the number of fields in a URL-encoded form body. Inserting a large number of repeated keys into a `MultiDict` took quadratic time on the event loop. ### Impact An attacker could block the event loop with a form POST within the default `client_max_size` to any handler that calls `Request.post()`. --- Patch: https://github.com/aio-libs/aiohttp/commit/615fec3d4f088f30d2ee72cad760152e92aa1c53 CVE: CVE-2026-128126
findings.title: AIOHTTP: Too many URL-encoded form fields block the event loop

findings.summary: ### Summary When reading a multipart part with `Content-Transfer-Encoding: base64`, `BodyPartReader.read_chunk()` kept reading until the chunk length was a multiple of 4, with no byte limit. A part with a short `Content-Length`, or a long run of whitespace, could cause the entire remaining body to be read into memory within a single call before any size check, or spin on the event loop.
findings.title: AIOHTTP: Base64 multipart parts bypass client_max_size

findings.summary: ### Summary The `max_msg_size` check in the WebSocket reader added the declared frame length to the size of the partial message already buffered. In the C extension this addition is 64-bit arithmetic, so a declared length close to 2**63 overflowed and the check passed. ### Impact An attacker could bypass `max_msg_size` and cause unbounded memory use by streaming an oversized WebSocket message after a small non-final fragment.
findings.title: AIOHTTP: WebSocket max_msg_size bypass via integer overflow

findings.summary: ### Summary While a request flagged as an upgrade (e.g. a WebSocket handshake) was being handled, all further data received on the connection was buffered with no size limit or flow control until the handler completed. ### Impact An attacker could cause unbounded memory use by streaming data behind an upgrade request to any handler that does not immediately accept or reject the upgrade.
findings.title: AIOHTTP: Unbounded buffering of data received during an upgrade request

findings.summary: ### Summary When the pipelined request queue was full, the pure-Python parser stored the unparsed remainder internally and also returned it to the caller. After a handler declined an upgrade request, the buffered data was re-fed, so the buffer grew with each handled request and already-handled requests were dispatched to the application again.
findings.title: AIOHTTP: Pure-Python parser request replay and buffer growth behind a declined upgrade

findings.summary: ### Summary When decompressing a payload made up of many concatenated compressed members (gzip, deflate or zstd), each member was decoded by passing the entire remaining input to a new decompressor, resulting in quadratic CPU time. Empty members produce no output, so `client_max_size` and output backpressure did not limit the work. ### Impact An attacker could block the event loop of a server with a specially crafted compressed request body or WebSocket message.
findings.title: AIOHTTP: Concatenated compressed streams cause excessive CPU use

findings.summary: ### Summary The WebSocket reader continued parsing frames already received after the receive queue had paused the transport, and empty messages were not counted towards the queue size. With permessage-deflate, a single read of compressed frames could add many megabytes of decompressed messages to the queue.
findings.title: AIOHTTP: WebSocket receive queue limits bypassed by small or compressed messages

findings.summary: ### Summary `Application.add_domain()` compiled each `*` in a host mask to `[^:]*`. With two or more wildcards in a mask, matching a long `Host` header that does not match the mask took polynomial time on the event loop. ### Impact An attacker could stall a server that registers a domain mask with more than one wildcard by sending requests with a long `Host` header. ### Workaround Use at most one `*` in a domain mask.
findings.title: AIOHTTP: Event loop stall in add_domain() wildcard matching

findings.summary: The Retadup USB worm is again being used to deliver malware to Windows systems, seven years after French authorities dismantled its botnet. The latest findings connect the worm to CoffeeLoader, a malware loader that uses graphics hardware during decryption and can download and run additional payloads on infected computers. The timeline needs an important distinction: Retadup’s infrastructure began returning in 2024, rather than suddenly reappearing in 2026.
findings.title: Retadup USB Worm Returns After 7 Years, Spreading CoffeeLoader Malware to Windows Systems

findings.summary: ## Summary `nltk.parse.dependencygraph.dot2img` invokes the Graphviz `dot` executable without the trusted-execution guarantees that NLTK applies to its other native-tool wrappers. The function resolves `dot` by bare name and then runs the resolved absolute path with a raw `subprocess.run`, omitting the ownership/writability check and the loader-environment scrub that `nltk.pathsec.spawn_trusted` provides.
findings.title: NLTK dot2img runs Graphviz 'dot' without the trusted-exec chokepoint, enabling local code execution via a writable PATH element

findings.summary: A Unicode normalization flaw allows attackers to bypass macOS file exclusion checks , affecting Deno, libarchive, HashiCorp go-slug, and Python setuptools across four CVEs. The flaw comes from two parts of the system disagreeing about what a file name is. Apple File System (APFS) resolves paths in a way that treats different Unicode spellings of one name as the same file. The affected tools compare paths as raw bytes.

findings.summary: Hackers are using a shipment-themed ZIP archive to launch a Windows malware chain that combines a legitimate signed application, DLL side-loading, and hidden Python code. The attack disguises its components as shipping material, images, documents, and a browser updater before running a payload linked to PureLogs and PureRAT infrastructure. The case shows why a trusted digital signature does not make an entire software package safe.

findings.summary: Hackers are hiding a backdoor named GraphDoor inside normal Microsoft and Ably traffic. The goal is to spy on government networks in Asia and Africa. The report also lists the plug-ins GraphDoor loads and points to Chinese-speaking threat groups as possible owners of the tools. GraphDoor first opens a named pipe built from its own process ID, in the form \\.\pipe\p%lu .

findings.summary: ## Summary CVE-2026-49283 / GHSA-6929-8p9f-26jx ("HTTP-Artifact TLS validator confusion allows cross-IdP authentication bypass") was fixed so that `HTTPArtifact::receive()` verifies the embedded SAML `Response` using the IdP metadata signing keys.

findings.summary: ### Summary A remote peer can stall a js-libp2p node's entire event loop for ~4–5 seconds per connection (and transiently allocate ~2 GB) by sending a ~15-byte crafted `publicKey` inside an Identify message. The malformed key reaches the DER decoder before any peer-id/signature check, so the attack is pre-auth and repeatable indefinitely by reconnecting.
findings.title: libp2p: ASN.1 DER decoder drives an unbounded synchronous loop on attacker-controlled length fields, stalling the Node event loop pre-auth

findings.summary: ### Summary A single gossipsub peer can grow a node's `topics` map without bound by flooding subscription RPCs, because the default configuration has no global, per-peer, or topic-length cap and peer scoring does not penalise subscription volume. The peer is never greylisted, so the growth continues toward OOM.
findings.title: libp2p: gossipsub creates a permanent topics-map entry per distinct subscription with no cap in the default config

This vulnerability can be triggered by sending a malformed Base64 input to affected JVMs, which can result in RCE. Details This vulnerability affects OpenJDK Java versions 17.0.6 and later running on x86-64 CPUs with AVX-512 VBMI (Vector Byte Manipulation Instructions) support enabled.

findings.summary: A critical flaw in OpenJDK’s Base64 decoder can let a remote attacker run code on an affected server without signing in. Oracle released security updates on November 17, 2026, and the U.S. Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency (CISA) urged organizations to patch immediately.

findings.summary: Apache’s HTTP/2 module, mod_http2, has a critical flaw tracked as CVE-2026-119618 that reportedly allows unauthenticated remote code execution. findings.summary: ReversingLabs has taken apart BubbleLoader, a loader that turns ordinary Windows programs into carriers for other malware. The attackers rewrite a handful of instructions at a program’s entry point, the spot where Windows begins running it, and add two PNG images that hold the hidden code. Known hosts include WinRAR, the x64dbg debugger, Windows Media Player, the Firefox launcher and virtiofs.

findings.summary: AuditTeam is an active threat group that uses the OpsAgent framework to compromise organizations across at least seven countries and territories. The campaign began in January 2026 and remained active through October 2026, at a minimum. In its ransom note, AuditTeam demands an “Audit & Consulting fee” in exchange for vulnerability reports. During this period, the group has infected dozens of organizations in Russia, Italy, the Philippines, Hong Kong, Senegal, Finland and China.
findings.title: The forced audit: how AuditTeam’s OpsAgent framework masks ransomware as consulting

findings.summary: A threat actor known as “tcherber” is selling and using stolen FortiGate VPN logins to get into company networks. The same person also builds custom malware, including a stealer, a remote desktop tool, and ransomware. The campaign shows how one weak VPN password can open the way to data theft and file encryption. The actor does not need a new Fortinet bug. Many of the logins come from guessing weak passwords, using default ones such as guest/guest and admin/admin, or reusing leaked ones.
findings.title: Hackers Use Stolen FortiGate VPN Credentials to Access Corporate Networks and Deploy Custom Malware

findings.summary: Hackers are using the logos of major defense and aerospace companies on a fake recruitment website to spread GravityRAT spyware. The site promises connections to overseas employers and offers an Android résumé builder that can steal text messages, location data, and files. Lockheed Martin, Airbus, and BAE Systems are among the brands displayed as supposed clients. Their logos are part of the lure, not evidence that the companies were breached or involved.

findings.summary: Hackers are targeting US trucking companies with fake freight portals, bogus carrier verification notices, and phony broker paperwork. Some sites collect fleet fuel card passwords and one-time codes. Others disguise malware as routine downloads, turning what appears to be a load confirmation or a terms update into a way to gain remote access to a Windows workstation. The campaigns target different people in the same business.
findings.title: Hackers Target US Trucking Companies With Fake Freight Portals to Steal Credentials and Deploy Malware

findings.summary: Java4Shell (CVE-2026-114938) is a memory corruption vulnerability in OpenJDK that lets malformed Base64 input write past the end of a heap array on servers with AVX-512 VBMI processors. Calif published its write-up on November 17, 2026, the same day Oracle and the OpenJDK project released fixes, and reported pre-authentication Remote Code Execution (RCE) against default installs of Jira, Confluence, Jenkins, Keycloak, JFrog Artifactory, and PingFederate.

findings.summary: Researchers have shown that a malicious cloud host can read and modify the memory of confidential virtual machines. They can also produce misleading attestation reports by exploiting a vulnerability in AMD Secure Encrypted Virtualization with Secure Nested Paging (SEV-SNP). This attack, known as Mior and tracked as CVE-2026-0462, targets the hardware protections meant to keep […]
findings.title: Mior Attack Breaks AMD SEV-SNP Security, Enabling Arbitrary Memory Access and Forged Attestation

findings.summary: An attack called Mior uses a graphics card to bypass AMD SEV-SNP , allowing access to confidential virtual machine memory, modification of guest memory, and making altered VMs appear to run trusted software. Tracked as CVE-2026-0462, the flaw carries a CVSS 4.0 score of 5.9. AMD Secure Encrypted Virtualization with Secure Nested Paging, or SEV-SNP, is designed to protect data while a virtual machine is running.
findings.title: Researchers Break AMD SEV-SNP Security to Read Encrypted Virtual Machine Memory Using a GPU

findings.summary: A four-year-old NVIDIA Linux GPU driver flaw , tracked as CVE-2026-47501 and dubbed ForgePtr, could let users with access to a vulnerable GPU take control of the entire server. The flaw allowed Stealthium researchers to gain root, the highest level of access on Linux, from inside an unprivileged container. The finding puts shared GPU servers used for AI training and inference at particular risk.
findings.title: 4-Year-Old NVIDIA Linux GPU Flaw Lets Users Hijack Entire Shared Servers

findings.summary: Google began rolling out Chrome 158 to Windows, macOS, and Linux on November 17, 2026, with 204 security fixes. The desktop release notes list six critical memory bugs that could lead to code execution . However, Google did not spell out the impact of each flaw. The patched builds are 158.0.8127.36 for Linux and 158.0.8127.36 or 158.0.8127.37 for Windows and macOS. Google said the update would reach users over the coming days and weeks. Three critical flaws are use-after-free bugs .

findings.summary: ## Summary atomic-server provisions a well-known invite at `{server}/setup` with `write = true`, `target` = the Drive root, and `usagesLeft = 1`. Invite redemption **ignores the redeemer's identity** (`for_agent: _` in `server/src/plugins/invite.rs:22`), so possession of the URL is the only requirement. An **unauthenticated** attacker who sends `GET /setup?public-key= ` has the server create a new Agent and grant it **write access to the entire Drive**.
findings.title: Atomic Server: Unauthenticated `/setup` invite grants write access to the entire Drive

findings.summary: ## Summary Atomic-Server exposes a `GET /bookmark` endpoint that fetches an attacker-supplied URL server-side, parses the response, and reflects the fetched content back to the caller. The endpoint requires no authentication and performs no authorization of its own, and the underlying fetch helper applies no allow-list or private-IP deny-list.
findings.title: Atomic Server: Unauthenticated full-response SSRF in Atomic-Server /bookmark endpoint

findings.summary: ## Summary The Commit apply path enforces **no allowlist of writable properties**, so any authenticated Agent can set the `internalId` string (datatype `string`, no character validation) on a resource it owns. The `/download` handler then uses that value **verbatim** as a filesystem path — `file_path.push(internal_id); NamedFile::open(file_path)` — with **no sanitization and no containment check** (`server/src/handlers/download.rs:56-65`).
findings.title: Atomic Server: Arbitrary file read via user-controlled `internalId` in the `/download` handler (leaks root agent private key)

findings.summary: ## Summary Files uploaded via `POST /upload` are served back by `GET /download/{path}` using `actix_files::NamedFile`. For `text/html` and `image/svg+xml`, actix-files (0.6.6) sets `Content-Disposition: inline`, so the browser **renders** the file instead of downloading it. The `/download` route sets **no `Content-Security-Policy`, no `X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff`, and no forced `attachment`** (CSP exists only on the SPA route), and files are served from the **same origin** as the app UI.
findings.title: Atomic Server: Stored XSS via uploaded files served inline (same-origin) on `/download` → account takeover

findings.summary: In altcha-org/altcha v2, the verifySolution method skips HMAC signature verification when the signature field is absent from the challenge payload, even when hmacSignatureSecret is configured. An attacker who strips the signature key from the challenge JSON passes the condition as false, bypassing tamper-detection entirely.
findings.title: ALTCHA PHP: verifySolution bypasses HMAC signature check when challenge signature is absent

findings.summary: ### Summary LLMKube's `ModelReconciler` accepts arbitrary absolute paths and `file://` URIs in the `Model.spec.source` field and propagates them to two distinct sinks without path allowlisting: (1) `os.Open()` inside the controller pod itself (`copyLocalModel`), and (2) a Kubernetes `HostPathVolumeSource` that mounts the attacker-supplied path into the inference pod's init container.
findings.title: LLMKube: Arbitrary Host File Read via Model.spec.source hostPath Injection

findings.summary: ## Description `bin/install-from-cache.js` downloads a prebuilt native addon (`*.node`) over the network and writes it directly to the artifact path **with no cryptographic integrity verification of any kind** — no checksum manifest, no signature, no SRI. A scan of the whole package for `createHash|sha256|checksum|integrity|digest|signature` finds nothing. The file is then `require()`-loaded by the consumer, which executes the addon's native module-init code.
findings.title: install-artifact-from-github loads downloaded native artifacts without integrity verification

findings.summary: ### Summary The `auth/aws` package of the `chainguard.dev/sdk` Go library provides Chainguard's AWS-backed identity federation (an AWS workload proves its identity to Chainguard by signing an AWS STS `GetCallerIdentity` request). Its verifier, `VerifyToken`, reads the `Chainguard-Audience` and `Chainguard-Identity` binding headers from a presented token but does not require them to be covered by the SigV4 signature.
findings.title: Chainguard SDK: AWS SigV4 token replay in auth/aws.VerifyToken — Chainguard-Audience/Chainguard-Identity binding headers not required in SignedHeaders

findings.summary: ### Summary The Miren Runtime RPC server (QUIC/HTTP3, default port `:8443`) requested TLS client certificates but never verified that a presented certificate chained to the cluster Certificate Authority. Because a client-certificate identity is granted a blanket RBAC bypass, any party able to reach the RPC listener could present a forged, self-signed certificate and be authenticated as a cluster **superuser** — no valid CA signature, credential, or prior authorization required.
findings.title: Miren Runtime: Authentication bypass in RPC layer: unverified TLS client certificates grant cluster superuser access

findings.summary: Several tools in `mssql-mcp-core` built T-SQL by string-interpolating caller-supplied identifiers and predicates directly into the statement passed to the node-mssql `Request.query()` batch API. Only data values were parameterized. Affected tools and inputs: - `update_data`, `delete_data`: `tableName` and the free-form `whereClause` were interpolated raw. - `insert_data`: `tableName` and column names (object keys) were interpolated raw.
findings.title: mssql-mcp-core: SQL injection in mssql-mcp write tools via unparameterized table names and WHERE clauses

findings.summary: ### Summary An architectural security boundary bypass in inline-detach and MessageInspector allows remote, unauthenticated attackers to force unbounded recursive decompression routines. By supplying a specially crafted OpenPGP message containing deeply nested compressed packet structures, an attacker can completely bypass the library's built-in DoS protections (MAX_LAYER_DEPTH = 16), leading to resource exhaustion, thread blocking, and potential Out-of-Memory (OOM) application crashes.
findings.title: PGPainless: Unbounded Compressed Packet Descent in inline-detach and MessageInspector leads to Denial of Service (DoS)

findings.summary: Hackers are actively exploiting a critical vulnerability in Apache Roller that lets them run code on affected servers without signing in, the Apache Software Foundation warned on November 17. The flaw, tracked as CVE-2026-129448, affects versions 4.0.0 through 6.1.4 and carries a CVSS 3.1 score of 9.8 out of 10. Apache says administrators should upgrade to Roller 6.1.6 or later. Version 6.1.5 is also vulnerable, but Apache tracks it under a separate CVE.

findings.summary: A financially motivated Windows malware campaign that uses Solana transaction memos to conceal the command-and-control (C2) addresses of the Overlord remote access trojan. Talos disclosed the activity on November 18 and tracks the operators as UAT-12643. Its assessment that the group is aligned with North Korea is low confidence, based on similarities to previously documented […]
findings.title: North Korea-Linked Hackers Hide Overlord RAT Server Addresses in Solana Blockchain Transactions

findings.summary: A suspected Chinese cyberespionage group has rebuilt its EggStreme malware framework, adding a Windows backdoor that waits for an incoming connection instead of calling out to an attacker-controlled server. Bitdefender’s November 18, 2026, report tracks the changes as the group continues to target government organizations in the Philippines. Researchers also found signs of possible targeting in Taiwan, but assessed that link with low to medium confidence.
findings.title: Chinese Hackers Upgrade EggStreme Malware With Silent Backdoor to Evade Security Detection

findings.summary: Splunk has released security updates for Splunk SOAR and Splunk Enterprise to fix a critical remote code execution flaw and a separate authentication bypass. The SOAR flaw, tracked as CVE-2026-131253, scored 9.9 out of 10 and requires an account with specific permissions. The Enterprise flaw, CVE-2026-76535, lets someone who has not signed in run searches under another user’s identity. The two bugs affect different products and require separate updates.

findings.summary: A North Korea-linked hacking group is using aNotepad, a free online note-sharing site, to control infected computers and swap malware on demand. The campaign targets South Korean policy and security professionals. It delivered the XenoRAT backdoor first and later a new JavaScript tool called NodeLinkRAT. findings.summary: Introduction For a threat actor, the perfect malware is one they don’t have to write, and already does all they need. One example of this is shown by the China-aligned APT known as Webworm, which has been known to deploy the open-source SoftEther VPN into the networks of compromised governmental organizations to maintain low-profile, long-term access.
findings.title: Spying on Governments with Zero Lines of Malware: A Custom SoftEther Bridge in Webworm’s Toolkit

findings.summary: ### Background NATS.io is a high performance open source pub-sub distributed communication technology, built for the cloud, on-premise, IoT and edge computing. The NATS Server supports MQTT clients and can bridge MQTT activity into NATS subjects across routes and leafnode connections. ### Problem Description An MQTT client could include protocol control characters in subscription filters that were later forwarded as NATS protocol data to route or leafnode connections.
findings.title: NATS Server: MQTT SUBSCRIBE Protocol Injection via Leaf Node/Route Forwarding allows arbitrary NATS command injection

findings.summary: ## What's wrong `verify_bundle` documents that it verifies "a bundle's DSSE envelope AND each per-claim signature", lists "per-claim signature failure" among its raised errors, and promises that partial verification never surfaces "an authenticated bundle that contains some invalid claims" as success. The code does not do this.
findings.title: Mareforma: verify_bundle never checks a per-claim signature

findings.summary: ### Summary `mareforma` 0.3.3 contains a critical integrity flaw in the REPLICATED convergence logic (`_maybe_update_replicated_unlocked()` in `mareforma/db/core.py:1300-1319`). The peer-selection SQL query that determines whether two independent claims "agree" on the same anchor does not verify that either claim carries a valid cryptographic signature from an enrolled validator key.
findings.title: Mareforma: Unsigned Claims Can Be Promoted to REPLICATED via Missing Signature Enforcement in Convergence Path

findings.summary: ### Summary jane-php (open-api-3) builds PHP via nikic/php-parser (AST), so string literals are escaped -- but PHPDoc comment text is emitted RAW. The generated Client/Endpoint method docblocks embed the header parameter name verbatim in a `@param array{ " "?: ... }` block. A `*/` in the header name closes the `/** ... */` docblock early and lands in class-body position; because the name is a raw string key (not identifier-mangled), the `*/` and following PHP survive.
findings.title: Jane: Instantiation RCE via header parameter name -> raw PHPDoc */ breakout (jane-php/open-api-3)

findings.summary: ### Summary jane-php (open-api-3) builds PHP via nikic/php-parser (AST), so string literals are escaped -- but PHPDoc comment text is emitted RAW. The generated Client/Endpoint method docblocks embed the parameter description verbatim in a `@param array{ " "?: ... }` block. A `*/` in the parameter description closes the `/** ... */` docblock early and lands in class-body position; because the name is a raw string key (not identifier-mangled), the `*/` and following PHP survive.
findings.title: Jane: Instantiation RCE via parameter description -> raw PHPDoc */ breakout (jane-php/open-api-3)

findings.summary: Broadcom has released fixes for five VMware flaws, and one lets anyone with network access to vCenter skip login. Broadcom published the advisory, VMSA-2026-0009 , on November 19, 2026. It covers vCenter, SDDC Manager, and VMware Tools. CVSS scores range from 6.7 to 9.8, and Broadcom has listed no workarounds. The most critical flaw is CVE-2026-123890 , an authentication bypass in the VMware Directory Service. It has a CVSS score of 9.8.

findings.summary: A new PHP attack dubbed phpAfterShell can lead to unauthenticated remote code execution on vulnerable servers, even if they have the October patches for PHP2Shell. Researchers at depthfirst disclosed the flaw on November 19 and demonstrated how it could be combined with a separate bug in PHP to run code remotely. The vulnerability, tracked as CVE-2026-126714 , has a CVSS v4.0 score of 9.2. The flaw sits in PHP’s default file-based session handler.
findings.title: New phpAfterShell Attack Bypasses PHP2Shell Fix to Enable Remote Code Execution

Today's PHP releases fix the flaw, called phpAfterShell. The flaw is tracked as CVE-2026-126714 and rated
findings.title: phpAfterShell Explained: How Hackers Could Turn a PHP Session Flaw Into Code Execution

findings.summary: The easiest way to fool someone is to give them something they already expect. A job offer. A message about a service outage. A familiar app. Nothing looks strange at first. And that's the problem. This week's stories show how ordinary things are being used to steal data, spread malware, and get people to hand over access. There's another shift worth watching. AI is making some attacks easier
findings.title: ThreatsDay: GPT-6.2 Jailbreak Flaws, BubbleLoader PNG Malware, $500M Ransom Demands + 17 More Stories

findings.summary: ### Summary axon rtk-install downloads a pre-built rtkx binary from GitHub releases and executes it via subprocess.run() on every text-compression call, without verifying its integrity — no checksum, signature, or attestation check anywhere in the download/install path.
findings.title: Axon: Download of Code Without Integrity Check in axon-mcp

findings.summary: The self-hosted `todoist-mcp-http` server accepts browser-origin MCP requests with attacker-controlled `Host` and `Origin` headers. A malicious website can use DNS rebinding to route its own origin to a victim's local `127.0.0.1` MCP server, then invoke Todoist MCP tools without a caller credential. This affects `github.com/Doist/todoist-mcp` at commit `d2903e0d945d2a559d71c091337ad6380511e62f`, package version `10.3.1`, when the optional Streamable HTTP server is running.
findings.title: Todoist MCP Server: Browser DNS rebinding lets websites write and delete Todoist data through local MCP server

findings.summary: The OpenAPI code generator (tapir-openapi-codegen-core) builds Scala source by string templating and emitted several names/values from the (untrusted) OpenAPI document without escaping or validation, allowing injection of arbitrary Scala that runs at generated-code compile time and/or endpoint-assembly time (build/codegen-time RCE from an attacker-controlled spec).
findings.title: Tapir: Construction/decode RCE via property name -> raw case-class field (tapir-openapi-codegen)

findings.summary: ### Summary Gortex is an MCP server exposing `write_file`, `edit_file`, and `move_inline` tools. `resolveFilePath` **exempts absolute paths** from confinement, and the write handlers — unlike `read_file` / `get_symbol_source` — **never call `guardSymlinkWithinRepo`**. A single MCP `write_file` call with an absolute path writes any file the daemon user can, **outside every indexed repo root** (`AtomicWriteFile`'s `MkdirAll` auto-creates missing parents).
findings.title: Gortex: Arbitrary file write / repo-confinement escape in `write_file` / `edit_file` / `move_inline` MCP tools → code execution

findings.summary: ## Summary `ChainBuilder` (the private RFC 5280 validator behind `TrustEvaluator` and the public credential-parsing API) terminated chain building on **Subject Distinguished Name string equality** rather than on cryptographic closure to a trust anchor. A certificate whose Subject DN string matched a trusted anchor's Subject DN was accepted as the chain terminus **with no signature verification** against the anchor's public key.
findings.title: OpenID4VP: X.509 chain validation accepts a forged certificate that reuses a trusted anchor's Subject DN without verifying its signature

findings.summary: ### Summary `keystore.Decode()` fails to check the error returned when reading the trailing SHA-1 integrity digest of a JKS keystore. If an attacker removes the final 20 bytes from a `.jks` file, the digest read returns an empty slice and the byte-comparison loop never executes, so `Decode()` returns the parsed keystore with `err == nil`.
findings.title: keystore-go: Keystore integrity and password verification bypass via stripped trailing digest in Decode()

findings.summary: A sandboxed iframe can auto-navigate itself via declarative refresh even when automatic features should be blocked. This allows attacker-controlled embedded content to redirect itself without user action. ### Summary Servo allows a sandboxed iframe to auto-navigate itself via declarative refresh in configurations that should block automatic features.
findings.title: Servo Sandbox bypass: declarative refresh can auto-navigate a sandboxed iframe

findings.summary: ### Impact The query REST API allows executing HQL queries to filter the listed pages. While this properly checks access rights for the current user, the query can be used to combine when clauses and blind queries, to recover values, through FROM clause injection to join BaseObject and StringProperty tables, bypassing the HQL validator's SELECT column whitelist.
findings.title: XWiki Platform: HQL injection in search allows unauthenticated database extraction including password hashes

findings.summary: ### Summary SharpIppNext's `IppProtocol.ReadIppRequestAsync()` unconditionally copies the entire attacker-supplied IPP document payload into an unbounded `MemoryStream` with no size limit.
findings.title: SharpIppNext: Unbounded IPP Document Stream Buffering Leads to Denial of Service

findings.summary: When obsidian-sync-mcp runs without MCP_AUTH_TOKEN (the documented no-auth mode for local use), the HTTP MCP endpoint does not validate the Host or Origin header before dispatching MCP methods (CWE-350).
findings.title: obsidian-sync-mcp: Missing Host/Origin validation lets a public website drive a victim's Obsidian vault via DNS rebinding (no-auth mode)

findings.summary: ### Summary An attacker who can supply a crafted SAML Response for parsing can crash a `gosaml2` service provider by sending an `EncryptedAssertion` with AES-GCM encryption metadata and a `CipherValue` shorter than the GCM nonce size (12 bytes). The library panics with `slice bounds out of range` before any validation completes.

findings.summary: ### Impact An unauthenticated request can occupy one synchronous application worker for seconds. findings.summary: ## Summary NLTK exposes a compile-time regular-expression denial of service in its regex-search helpers. When an application passes untrusted text as the search pattern to `TokenSearcher.findall()` / `Text.findall()`, or as the tokenizer pattern to `RegexpTokenizer`, the pattern is handed to the third-party `regex` engine, whose compilation cost is roughly quadratic in the number of capturing groups.
findings.title: NLTK: Compile-time regex DoS in NLTK search/tokenizer sinks: quadratic regex-engine compile bypasses the match-only timeout

findings.summary: ## Summary `Prover9Parent.config_prover9(binary_location=...)` (and `Mace`, which inherits it) accepts a relative `binary_location` and passes it as `path_to_bin` to `find_binary`, which disables the CWD-relative rejection guard. Unlike the boxer/senna/malt/repp siblings, prover9/mace apply no `os.path.isabs()` filter, so the resolved relative program path (e.g. `./prover9`) is executed from the current working directory via `subprocess.Popen`.

findings.summary: ### Summary The recursive traversal engines behind WordNetCorpusReader's Synset.tree() and Synset.acyclic_tree() have no maximum call-depth safeguard and default to unlimited depth. They guard against literal cycles, but not against a long, genuinely acyclic relation chain — which exhausts the Python call stack the same way as the sibling DependencyGraph finding I reported separately.
findings.title: Natural Language Toolkit (NLTK): Uncontrolled recursion (crash DoS) in Synset.tree()/acyclic_tree() via WordNet relation traversal

findings.summary: ## Summary NLTK ships a security wrapper, `nltk.pathsec.ZipFile`, that is meant to confine archive extraction to trusted data roots and to block link-based escapes. findings.summary: ### Summary Refitter emits the spec's content-type key (content map key in requestBody/responses) verbatim into a Refit `[Headers("Accept: ", "Content-Type: ")]` attribute string without escaping `"`. A crafted value survives Refitter's default OpenAPI validation, breaks out of the attribute and the enclosing interface + namespace, injects a top-level `file class` with a `[ModuleInitializer]` method, and reopens so the file stays valid.
findings.title: Refitter allows arbitrary code execution through unescaped OpenAPI content-type values

findings.summary: ### Summary Refitter emits the spec's header parameter name (parameters[].name with in: header) verbatim into a Refit `[Header(" ")]` attribute string without escaping `"`. A crafted value survives Refitter's default OpenAPI validation, breaks out of the attribute and the enclosing interface + namespace, injects a top-level `file class` with a `[ModuleInitializer]` method, and reopens so the file stays valid.
findings.title: Refitter allows code execution through unescaped OpenAPI header parameter names

findings.summary: ### Summary Refitter emits each OpenAPI path (the paths-object key) verbatim into a Refit `[Get(" ")]` attribute string, without escaping `"` or restricting characters. A crafted single-line, /-prefixed path survives Refitter's default OpenAPI validation yet closes the attribute string and the enclosing interface + namespace, injects a top-level `file class` with a `[ModuleInitializer]` method, and reopens a namespace + interface so the file stays valid.
findings.title: Refitter allows arbitrary code execution through unescaped OpenAPI paths

findings.summary: ## Summary `http.paginate` validates only the initial `base_url`, then follows server-supplied pagination targets (RFC 5988 `Link: rel="next"` headers, cursor/offset URLs) in a loop **without revalidating each follow-up URL**. An attacker's first-page response can point `next` at an internal address, causing a second-order SSRF whose internal body is aggregated into the returned items. ## Root Cause `src/core/modules/atomic/http/paginate.py:495` validates `base_url` (first URL only).
findings.title: Flyto2 Core: http.paginate follows server-supplied next-page URLs (Link header / cursor) without SSRF revalidation

findings.summary: ## Summary `validate_url_ssrf` resolves the hostname, checks the IP against private ranges, then **discards the IP and returns the hostname URL string**. aiohttp performs a fresh, independent DNS resolution at connect time. An attacker controlling DNS for a hostname (TTL 0, alternating public IP and internal IP) passes validation on the first lookup and connects to the internal IP on the second — a classic check-then-use race.
findings.title: Flyto2 Core: SSRF guard validates the resolved IP but connects by hostname, allowing DNS-rebinding TOCTOU

findings.summary: ## Summary django-docutils before `0.30.0` rendered reStructuredText through Docutils without protected web-safe defaults. Public rendering paths, including `publish_doctree`, `publish_html_from_source`, `publish_html_from_doctree`, `publish_parts_from_doctree`, the `{% rst %}` template tag, the `rst` template filter, `DocutilsTemplates`, and `DocutilsView`, could process attacker-controlled RST with Docutils directives that read local files, fetch URL-backed content, or emit raw HTML.
findings.title: django-docutils unsafe Docutils defaults allow local file disclosure, SSRF, and stored XSS

findings.summary: ### Summary jane-php resolves external `$ref` targets at code-generation time via `file_get_contents($ref)` (jane-php/json-schema-runtime/Reference.php::doResolve) with no scheme/path restriction. An attacker-controlled OpenAPI document can therefore cause: `$ref: 'http://attacker/x'` -> SSRF (HTTP GET at gen time; response inlined = RFI); `$ref: '/abs/file'` -> LFI; `$ref: '../secret.yaml'` -> path-traversal LFI (CWE-22, arbitrary local JSON/YAML read).
findings.title: Jane: $ref resolution performs SSRF + LFI (path traversal) at code-generation time (jane-php)

findings.summary: ### Summary Daptin registers a generic WebSocket endpoint, `GET /yjs/:documentName`, for real-time collaborative document editing (YJS/CRDT). Unlike its purpose-built sibling route, this generic endpoint performs no per-resource authorization check - it only verifies that *some* user session exists.
findings.title: Daptin: Broken Access Control (IDOR) in the generic YJS collaboration endpoint

findings.summary: ### Summary An unauthenticated attacker can inject arbitrary SQL through the `sort` query parameter accepted by Daptin's generic entity list endpoint (`GET /api/ `), which every table in a Daptin instance exposes.
findings.title: Daptin: Unauthenticated SQL Injection via the `sort` query parameter on every entity list endpoint

findings.summary: Standalone `streamable-http` mode in `datalayer/jupyter-mcp-server` rejects forged `Host` and `Origin` headers on `/mcp`, but custom management routes mounted on the same application do not get the same browser-origin protection. A malicious website can keep an attacker origin while its hostname resolves to `127.0.0.1` or a private target address, then send `PUT /api/connect` to replace the MCP server's active Jupyter backend.
findings.title: Jupyter MCP Server: Browser DNS rebinding can hijack the Jupyter backend through management routes

findings.summary: Standalone `streamable-http` mode in `datalayer/jupyter-mcp-server` requires `MCP_TOKEN` for `/mcp`, but the custom management routes mounted on the same application do not enforce that token. An unauthenticated network caller can invoke `PUT /api/connect`, choose the Jupyter backend URL and token fields, reset the server context, and make the MCP server start a kernel client against attacker-controlled infrastructure.
findings.title: Jupyter MCP Server: Unauthenticated management routes can hijack the Jupyter backend in standalone HTTP mode

findings.summary: A crafted PNG can make `imagemeta.Decode` allocate memory far in excess of the input file's size, leading to memory exhaustion. Two separate paths in the `zTXt` "Raw profile type iptc" branch are affected: the declared chunk length drives an allocation directly, and the embedded zlib stream is decompressed without an output bound. A 42-byte file allocated 256 MB, and a 127 KB file allocated 460 MB.
findings.title: bep/imagemeta: Unbounded memory allocation decoding PNG `zTXt` "Raw profile type iptc" chunks

findings.summary: ### Summary The security patch introduced in baserCMS 5.2.3 to address CVE-2026-30940 / [GHSA-c5c6-37vq-pjcq](https://github.com/baserproject/basercms/security/advisories/GHSA-c5c6-37vq-pjcq) is **incomplete**. The patch added a `realpath()`-based directory traversal check in `BcThemeFileService::getFullpath()`, but the check is **entirely skipped** when `realpath($baseDir)` returns `false` — which occurs whenever the target subdirectory does not physically exist on disk.

findings.summary: ### Summary The security patch introduced in baserCMS 5.2.3 to address CVE-2026-30940 / [GHSA-c5c6-37vq-pjcq](https://github.com/baserproject/basercms/security/advisories/GHSA-c5c6-37vq-pjcq) is **incomplete**. The patch added a `realpath()`-based directory traversal check in `BcThemeFileService::getFullpath()`, but the check is **entirely skipped** when `realpath($baseDir)` returns `false` — which occurs whenever the target subdirectory does not physically exist on disk.
findings.title: baserCMS: Path Traversal Bypass via realpath() in BcThemeFileService (CVE-2026-30940 Patch Bypass)

findings.summary: ### Summary An unauthenticated path‑traversal / arbitrary file read vulnerability in Etherpad's /static/* handler allows any remote, unauthenticated user to read any file on the server's filesystem (e.g. GET /static/plugins/ep_etherpad-lite/static/..%5C..%5C..%5C..%5C..%5C..%5C..%5Cetc/passwd returns /etc/passwd) available to the user running the etherpad software. Because the endpoint is mounted before the authentication middleware, no credentials, session, or configuration change are required.

findings.summary: Around 8.8 million NGINX services may still be open to the NGINX2Root flaws. Censys live tracker counts 8,823,450 services that run an affected version and offer HTTP/2. Each bug sits in an NGINX worker process and needs a specific feature to be switched on.

findings.summary: Drupal released security updates on November 18 to fix a critical flaw that could let attackers take over vulnerable websites without logging in. The bug, tracked as CVE-2026-132165, affects the installer included with Drupal core. Under specific conditions, an attacker could use it to attempt to reinstall an existing site, leading to a takeover or remote code execution (RCE). Drupal urges administrators to update immediately. The installer is designed to set up new Drupal sites.

findings.summary: A heap buffer overflow in OpenSSL’s Base64 encoding function can corrupt application memory when the library processes very large inputs. The flaw, tracked as CVE-2026-121481, was published on November 18, 2026, with a critical CVSS 3.1 score of 9.8. That score describes the potential severity, but it does not mean every service that uses OpenSSL is remotely exposed. The bug affects EVP_EncodeBlock() , which converts binary data into printable text.

findings.summary: The Apache Software Foundation has disclosed a critical flaw in Apache Tomcat that allows a remote attacker to join a trusted server cluster without authentication. Tracked as CVE-2026-133325, the flaw affects clusters that use TLS 1.3 with a pre-shared key. Apache published the advisory on November 19, 2026, and credited researcher Mike Read with finding the issue. The Apache Tomcat 11 security advisory identifies versions 11.0.28 and 11.0.29 as affected.

findings.summary: ### Summary Refitter (the `refitter` dotnet tool, built on NJsonSchema for `$ref` resolution) fetches remote `http(s)` URLs and reads local files (including absolute paths and `../` traversal outside the input directory), inlining the referenced schema into the generated Refit interface/contracts. Running `refitter --output Out.cs` on a spec whose `$ref` points at an attacker/internal URL or an arbitrary local file yields SSRF, remote file inclusion, and local file inclusion.
findings.title: Refitter: Unrestricted OpenAPI references permit build-host SSRF and file inclusion

findings.summary: ## Summary The Appium storage plugin exposes an HTTP endpoint `POST /storage/delete` that takes a user-supplied `name` and deletes it from the server storage folder. The handler passes `name` straight into `path.join(storageRoot, name)` and then `fs.rimraf()` **without any path sanitization**.
findings.title: appium allows unauthenticated arbitrary file/directory deletion in @appium/storage-plugin

A single client can freeze the entire broker by sending one specially crafted `SUBSCRIBE` packet followed by one `PUBLISH` packet. The vulnerability is caused by two defects: 1.
findings.title: aMQTT: Inefficient Regular Expression Complexity and Uncontrolled Resource Consumption and Improper Input Validation

findings.summary: The defect ---------- Confirmed at HEAD. server.go: cmdXCLIENT = []byte("XCLIENT") is 7 bytes (line 78), so the dispatch match cmdXCLIENT.match(cmd) only guarantees len(input) >= 7. The handler then slices input[8:] (line 586): case sc.XClientOn && cmdXCLIENT.match(cmd): if toks := bytes.Split(input[8:], []byte{' '}); len(toks) > 0 { // line 586 A client sending the bare command XCLIENT (exactly 7 bytes) hits input[8:7] and panics runtime error: slice bounds out of range [8:7].
findings.title: go-guerrilla crashes on a bare XCLIENT command (7-byte slice off-by-one panic)

findings.summary: ### Impact After receiving an HTTP redirection, Git LFS may forward certain HTTP headers to a host other than the one for which they were intended. While `Authorization` headers are never forwarded to inappropriate hosts, `Cookie` headers may be forwarded incorrectly. Git LFS has resolved this issue by never forwarding `Cookie` headers to hosts other than the ones for which they were intended.
findings.title: Git LFS may leak HTTP headers after redirections

findings.summary: ### Impact When Git LFS makes object transfer or authentication requests to a remote host via SSH, it passes the path component of the remote's SSH URL as part of a command to be executed, but does not properly format the URL's path component as a single argument. By inserting shell meta-characters into the SSH URL, an attacker may be able to execute arbitrary commands on the remote host, if the host passes the commands to a shell without sanitizing them first.
findings.title: Git LFS may attempt arbitrary remote commands via crafted SSH URLs

findings.summary: ## Summary Route selection uses the raw un-normalized request path, and the per-route ACL and basic-auth gates hang off that selection, so a dot-segment, encoded-dot, or double-slash variant of a protected path selects a different route, skips both gates, and is forwarded to the backend which normalizes and serves the protected resource. Unauthenticated; complete bypass of the access control the operator configured. Confirmed at HEAD b841544.
findings.title: Fabio: Access-control bypass through unnormalized request paths

findings.summary: ### Impact `amqtt` is vulnerable to a remote denial of service caused by incomplete MQTT QoS 2 transactions remaining allocated after the associated client disconnects. MQTT QoS 2 uses a four-step handshake to provide exactly-once delivery. If a client begins a QoS 2 transaction but disconnects before the handshake completes, `amqtt` retains the associated transaction state and packet identifier without an expiration mechanism to remove it.
findings.title: aMQTT: Denial of Service (DoS) via Memory Leak in Unmanaged QoS 2 Session Handshakes

findings.summary: ### Summary The email second factor is an mt_rand() six-digit code verified with no attempt limit or lockout The email second factor is a six-digit code drawn from `mt_rand()` and verified with no attempt limit, so an attacker who already has the password can brute-force it inside its validity window.
findings.title: Poweradmin: The email second factor is an mt_rand() six-digit code verified with no attempt limit or lockout, so an attacker holding the password can brute-force it within the validity window

findings.summary: ### Impact When fetching objects from a malicious repository, Git LFS may execute an arbitrary command or binary after failing to sufficiently restrict the set of configuration options defined in an `.lfsconfig` file in the repository.
findings.title: Git LFS may execute arbitrary commands via crafted Git LFS configurations

findings.summary: ### Impact When fetching objects from a malicious repository, Git LFS may execute an arbitrary command or binary after incorrectly parsing the Git configuration options defined for a submodule. Git LFS reads Git configuration options without checking for embedded line-ending control characters. By inserting control characters such as line feed (LF) into certain values, an attacker may be able to mimic options that cause Git LFS to execute an arbitrary command when fetching or adding objects.
findings.title: Git LFS may execute arbitrary commands via crafted Git configurations

findings.summary: ## Description ### Summary On a self-hosted, single-tenant Budibase instance (`multiTenancy:false`), the public bootstrap endpoint `POST /api/global/users/init` remains fully exploitable **after** the instance has been provisioned. Its "already initialised" guard (`checkAnyUserExists()`) is evaluated inside a **tenant-scoped** database context derived from an **attacker-controlled `tenantId`** in the request body.

findings.summary: # Summary `svg2rlg()` expands ` ` references without any limit on the total number of expansions. Only direct cycles are rejected (`CircularRefError`). A group containing N ` ` elements that point to another such group multiplies the work by N per nesting level, so an SVG of about 1.4 KB makes svglib clone and render over 100,000 nodes, taking tens of seconds of CPU time and hundreds of MiB of memory. Each additional level adds about 245 bytes to the document and multiplies time by ~10.
findings.title: svglib: Exponential resource consumption via nested <use> references in svg2rlg
